frequency_question: How often do complex bilateral trade negotiations between major non-aligned economic powers successfully result in a signed agreement within a defined multi-year window?
membership_rule: Includes formal, high-level bilateral or plurilateral trade agreement negotiations between major economies (e.g., US, EU, India, Mercosur, ASEAN) that faced domestic ratification hurdles, regulatory harmonization gaps, or labor/environmental standard disputes. Excludes minor tariff-only updates or bilateral deals concluded under extreme geopolitical duress or wartime conditions.
coverage_note: 3 named; representative of high-level bilateral trade negotiations between major economies with divergent regulatory standards.
known_gaps: Excludes smaller regional pacts where political alignment overpowered regulatory friction.
skeleton: Named specific modern complex trade negotiations between major asymmetric or symmetric economies since 2000, tracking whether deep-content agreements reached formal signature within a targeted multi-year window.
multiplier: 3 cases evaluated directly against historical friction baselines
validity_reason: Global trade architectures, protectionist pressures, and regulatory divergence trends remain stable across this timeframe.
